title: Semilinear diagram naturality of strict finite-fibre restrictions
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a scheme $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the strict derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $Rf_*$ be the tower direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

For a geometric point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], set $S=X\times_Ys$ with projections $v:S\to X$, $h:S\to s$ [def-pc-base-change], and $P_y=\{x:s\to X\mid fx=y\}$. For $x\in P_y$ let $i_x:s\to S$ be the unique lift, so $vi_x=x$ and $hi_x=\operatorname{id}_s$. This is a finite set; an empty sum indexed by $P_y$ is the zero object. Write $L(-)^*$ for the completed integral pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $(-)_n^*$ for its exact finite-coefficient inverse image.

Let $\sigma:k\xrightarrow{\sim}k$ be a field automorphism and let $u:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X'$, $w:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y'$ be scheme isomorphisms semilinear over $\sigma$, where $X',Y'$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f':X'\to Y'$ is finite with $f'u=wf$. Transport the point to $y'=wy\sigma_s^{-1}:s\to Y'$, where $\sigma_s$ is the induced scheme automorphism of $s$. Then $S=X\times_Ys$ is carried isomorphically to $S'=X'\times_{Y'}s$, and $P_y$ is bijective with $P_{y'}$ by $x\mapsto x'=ux\sigma_s^{-1}$. Use the induced equivalences of coefficient sheaf categories, the same coefficient ring $\mathcal O_E$, and the canonical completed pullback composition comparisons of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Transport $K$ on $X$ to $K'$ on $X'$ by the equivalence inverse to $u^*$.

For one flat-term K-flat representative and its strict quotients, write $b_n$ for finite exchange and $r_{n,x}$ for the $x$-component of the counit-germ restriction
$$y_n^*f_{*,n}K_n\xrightarrow{b_n}h_{*,n}v_n^*K_n\xrightarrow{(r_{n,x})_x}\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}x_n^*K_n.$$
The induced transport comparisons carry $b_n$ to $b'_n$ and $r_{n,x}$ to $r'_{n,x'}$ as maps of strict quotient complexes. These equalities commute with every quotient transition, countable product, Roos differential and projection; the completed pullback composition comparisons are normalized by those same finite-level composition maps. Thus they identify the two corresponding natural maps in the completed derived category over $s$ before point sections.

The equalities remain valid under raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], point sections and passage to the common-stage category [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. On the direct sum the transport is precisely permutation by $x\mapsto x'$ together with the induced stalk transport on each summand [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. The comparisons are natural in morphisms of input complexes: $a(m|_{i_x})=a(m)|_{i_x}$ for every sheaf morphism $a$. The case $\sigma=\operatorname{id}_k$ gives naturality for ordinary diagram isomorphisms; no compatibility of $\sigma$ with $k_0$ is required.

proof.text: Use the normalized geometric constructions and strict-system comparisons of the diagram models. Apply strict transport to obtain the source, middle and sum isomorphisms and both commuting strict complex squares. Finiteness of the point sets is finitePoints.

Apply level evaluation to each strict square. Apply the three functors defining roos, and the localization and total-limit functors defining completed. Functor.map_commSq proves every resulting square; the actual four arrows are retained by Square.image.

For c,u,w and the fibre isomorphism use podReindexingCompletionUnit to obtain their PodCompletionReindex laws. The coefficient prime is a unit in each residue field by the finite-field characteristic and the structure map to Spec k.

On a flat-term K-flat reduction presentation apply constructible vertices to obtain the full-subcategory witnesses hB and hR. Restrict each completed commutative square by ObjectProperty.hom_ext. Apply raw rationalization and pointRationalFibre, using functorial preservation of CommSq each time.

Input naturality is naturality of b,r and the component transformations. For common-stage squares, apply the completed clauses at the coefficient model, restrict to constructibles, then apply rationalization, the actual stage inclusion and pointQbarFibre.
